Compute mean length-at-age

get_growth.Rd

Computes mean length at each modeled age under one of three growth curves, selected by growth_model: the Schnute parameterization of the von Bertalanffy (VB) curve, the Richards curve, or the growth cessation model.

Usage

get_growth(
  n_age,
  A1,
  A2,
  L1 = NULL,
  L2 = NULL,
  log_k = NULL,
  min_age = 1L,
  log_k_mult = NULL,
  k_mult_ages = NULL,
  plus_group_adjust = FALSE,
  growth_model = "vonB",
  b = NULL,
  L0 = NULL,
  log_rmax = NULL,
  log_k_gc = NULL,
  t50 = NULL,
  age_offset = 0
)

Arguments

n_age

Integer. Number of age classes.

A1

Integer. Reference age for L1 (data).

A2

Integer. Reference age for L2 (data).

L1

Numeric. Length at age A1 (may be AD). Used by "vonB" and "richards".

L2

Numeric. Length at age A2 (may be AD). Used by "vonB" and "richards".

log_k

Numeric. Log growth coefficient per model age step (may be AD). Used by "vonB" and "richards".

min_age

Integer. Minimum age (default 1L).

log_k_mult

Numeric vector (may be AD). Log K multipliers; NULL or length zero retains the single-K curve. "vonB" only.

k_mult_ages

Integer vector (data). Ages at which the multipliers apply, strictly increasing within the modeled ages and matching log_k_mult. "vonB" only.

plus_group_adjust

Logical (data). Apply SS3's oldest-age length approximation, independently of the multipliers (default FALSE). "vonB" only.

growth_model

Character (data). Growth curve: "vonB" (default), "richards" or "cessation". See Details.

b

Numeric. Richards shape parameter on the natural scale (may be AD). Must be non-zero. Used by "richards".

L0

Numeric. Length at absolute age 0, natural scale (may be AD). Used by "cessation".

log_rmax

Numeric. Log maximum growth rate, in length per model age step (may be AD). Used by "cessation".

log_k_gc

Numeric. Log steepness of the logistic decline in growth rate, per model age step (may be AD). Used by "cessation".

t50

Numeric. Absolute age at the logistic midpoint (may be AD). Used by "cessation".

age_offset

Numeric (data). Added to the modeled ages to give the absolute age t used by "cessation" (default 0).

Value

Numeric vector of length n_age: mean length at each age a = min_age, ..., min_age + n_age - 1.

Details

Growth models

growth_modelCurveArguments used
"vonB" (default)Schnute VBL1, L2, log_k (optionally log_k_mult, k_mult_ages, plus_group_adjust)
"richards"RichardsL1, L2, log_k, b
"cessation"Growth cessationL0, log_rmax, log_k_gc, t50, age_offset

Stock Synthesis (SS3) GrowthModel 3 (age-specific K) is reproduced by "vonB" with log_k_mult and k_mult_ages.

All rates (log_k, log_rmax and log_k_gc) are per model age step.

von Bertalanffy (growth_model = "vonB")

Uses the Schnute parameterization of the von Bertalanffy growth curve, $$L_a = L_1 + (L_2 - L_1)\frac{1 - e^{-k(a - A_1)}}{1 - e^{-k(A_2 - A_1)}}.$$ Optionally reproduces SS3 GrowthModel 3 (age-specific K), including its cumulative multipliers and plus-group approximation.

Multipliers apply cumulatively: K at age a is the base K times the product of all multipliers at ages less than or equal to a. The final K carries forward. Linf is derived from L1, L2, A1 and A2 using the oldest-age K; growth from age a to a+1 uses K at a. Consequently, with multipliers the curve need not pass through L2 at A2. A1 must be a modeled age for this option. Below A1, opal retains base-K exponential growth toward this Linf; SS3 instead uses a linear segment.

The plus-group approximation averages a linear increase from the oldest length to Linf over a further max_age ages, with weights exp(-0.2)^j, j = 0, ..., max_age. The fixed 0.2 is not mortality; this option requires a positive integer oldest age.

log_k is the log rate per model age unit, whereas SS3 reads an annual rate and scales by season duration. For a quarterly age step, use log(K_SS3 * 3/12); multipliers are dimensionless. This reimplementation is pinned to SS3 v3.24AB beginning-of-season lengths; later SS3 versions may differ. CV interpolation is handled separately by get_sd_at_age.

Richards (growth_model = "richards")

Uses the Richards (1959) curve as parameterized by Schnute (1981), $$L_a = \left[L_1^b + (L_2^b - L_1^b)\frac{1 - e^{-k(a - A_1)}}{1 - e^{-k(A_2 - A_1)}}\right]^{1/b}.$$ The parameterization and the guidance in this subsection follow the Stock Synthesis user manual (section 8.5.2.2.2, Richards growth function). See the Richards growth vignette on the Stock Synthesis website for further technical guidance.

b = 1 gives the VB curve. As b approaches 0, the curve approaches the Gompertz curve; Gompertz growth can be obtained by fixing b at a small value such as 1e-4. b is a floating-point parameter on the natural scale that may be positive or negative but not exactly 0. If its initial value is non-zero, there is effectively no risk of an estimated b landing exactly on 0.

When A1 is greater than the youngest modeled age, some parameter combinations give undefined (NaN) predicted lengths at the younger ages. Below A1 the fraction in the equation is negative, so with b > 0 the bracket can become negative. With b < 0 the asymptotic bracket can be zero or negative, in which case Linf is undefined. The choice of A1 and A2 also constrains the possible curve shapes. opal does not clamp the bracket.

Growth cessation (growth_model = "cessation")

Uses the growth cessation model of Maunder et al. (2018), Eq. 2, $$L_t = L_0 + r_{max}\left[\frac{\ln(e^{-k t_{50}} + 1) - \ln(e^{k(t - t_{50})} + 1)}{k} + t\right],$$ with rmax = exp(log_rmax) and k = exp(log_k_gc). The growth rate declines logistically from rmax, with midpoint age t50. L(0) = L0, and the asymptotic length is \(L_0 + r_{max}[\ln(e^{-k t_{50}} + 1)/k + t_{50}]\). As k approaches 0, the curve approaches L0 + rmax * t / 2. Both log terms are computed as an overflow-safe \(\log(1 + e^x)\) (RTMB::logspace_add for AD inputs), which avoids overflow for large k * (t - t50).

Unlike the VB and Richards curves, which depend only on a - A1, this curve depends on absolute age t, so the age origin matters. t is the modeled age plus age_offset. For example, if model age 1 corresponds to biological age 0, use age_offset = -1.

References

Maunder, M.N., Deriso, R.B., Schaefer, K.M., Fuller, D.W., Aires-da-Silva, A.M., Minte-Vera, C.V. and Campana, S.E. (2018). The growth cessation model: a growth model for species showing a near cessation in growth with application to bigeye tuna (Thunnus obesus). Marine Biology 165: 76. doi:10.1007/s00227-018-3336-9 .

Methot, R.D. Jr. and Wetzel, C.R. (2013). Stock synthesis: A biological and statistical framework for fish stock assessment and fishery management. Fisheries Research 142: 86–99. doi:10.1016/j.fishres.2012.10.012 .

Methot, R.D. Jr., Wetzel, C.R., Taylor, I.G., Doering, K.L., Perl, E.F. and Johnson, K.F. Stock Synthesis User Manual, Version 3.30.25.1. NOAA Fisheries, Seattle, WA. Section 8.5.2.2.2, Richards growth function. https://nmfs-ost.github.io/ss3-doc/SS330_User_Manual_release.html.

Richards, F.J. (1959). A flexible growth function for empirical use. Journal of Experimental Botany 10: 290–301.

Schnute, J. (1981). A versatile growth model with statistically stable parameters. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 38: 1128–1140.
